now.v: Mnemosyne had eight fact stores that all kinda did the same job. Bugs everywhere. I’m merging them into one ledger. It’s surgery.
Synapse. Same problem, way less stuff. It only cares about two numbers: speed and cost.
Both of them against LongMemEval. Vibes are not a metric.
Lunch & learns at work on Claude. Memory, artifacts, video. Goal: the whole company shows up.
Weird web behavior, for a talk. I’d rather build a tiny broken version than read another tutorial.

chapters.b: First thing people actually used: a Go tool that pulls 20,000+ V2Ray configs, dedupes them and rebuilds the list every 6 hours. One run takes 11 seconds. 130 stars. Wild. That’s when speed became my whole personality.

Next I got into networks that don’t want to be mapped. Wrote a scanner that pokes Cloudflare and Fastly edges and flags DPI tricks and MITM. Built a live dashboard that tracks internet shutdowns in Iran. Some code matters more than the rest.
December 2025. Computer Programming at Algonquin College. Graduated. My curiosity didn’t. It got worse.
Then I noticed AI agents forget everything. Felt like a bug in the universe. Now most of my days go to memory systems, local-first stuff and open source. No regrets. Mostly.

loves.b: Your data. Your disk. If it needs someone else’s server to remember your name, it’s rented.
No benchmark? Then it’s a guess. Learned that one the hard way. It’s in my writing.
Runtimes, compilers, networking, databases, Unicode and RTL text. The “wait, why does it do that?” stuff.
Reading other people’s code is the fastest way to get humbled. Love it.

projects.name: mnemosyne
projects.story: AI agents have goldfish memory. Mnemosyne gives them one that lives on your laptop. Then I benchmarked it. Ouch. Conflict resolution scored 50% and 25% on BEAM. Facts were scattered across eight overlapping stores. Lowkey embarrassing. Now: one fact ledger, conflicts that pick a winner, trust scores in every recall.

projects.name: synapse
projects.story: Mnemosyne’s leaner sibling. Write memory in, embed locally, answer by retrieval. The hard part: making agents check memory before they reply. Rules files are just suggestions. So it uses tool_choice and hooks instead.

projects.name: memory evals
projects.story: LongMemEval as the main test. LoCoMo got dropped: about 6.4% of its answer key is wrong. Grading against a broken key is just grading yourself.

projects.name: v2go
projects.story: Grabs 20,000+ V2Ray configs, dedupes them, rebuilds the list every 6 hours. 11 seconds a run. Go was the right call.

projects.name: cf-knife
projects.story: A pocket knife for networks that hate being mapped. Probes Cloudflare and Fastly edges over TLS and HTTP. Flags DPI tricks and MITM.

projects.name: iran-internet-monitor
projects.story: Live dashboard tracking connectivity and censorship in Iran. When the internet goes dark, somebody should be counting.

projects.name: syncodoro
projects.story: A Pomodoro timer that works offline and syncs when you’re back. Stats on top, so you see how locked in you really were. Usually less than you think.

projects.name: free-macos
projects.story: macOS never shipped Linux’s free command. So now it does. Live memory stats, right in your terminal.

projects.name: netray
projects.story: Network diagnostics in Go. Small. Sharp. No fluff.

projects.name: fts5 deep dive
projects.story: Rebuilt full-text search on SQLite FTS5. Benchmarked it on a million docs. 300–460× faster. Full story in my writing.

experience.b: Architecture, roadmap, and the bugs nobody else wants.
Memory tools agents check before every answer. Even when they’d rather not.
Shipping at work. Also running company-wide lunch & learns on Claude.
Go tools, network scanners, PWAs. Lately the AI memory + LLM tooling world.
Graduated. Kept building way past the assignment.

title: boo. i’m dani.
i give ai agents a memory.
body: Every AI agent you’ve used forgets you the second the tab closes. Every. Single. One.
That bugs me way more than it should. So I’m building them a memory that lives on your laptop, not in a data center. Open source. Local-first. Still a little broken. Getting there.
